## Q12 — the Gulf states (sub-questions)

The Gulf is a distinct analytical focus because the standard frame (the GCC as a single bloc) does not fit the observed behavior.

| # | Sub-question | Status |
|---|---------------|--------|
| Q12.1 | How should the Gulf neighbors be sub-grouped? | drafted |
| Q12.2 | How did each sub-group's strategy evolve from JCPOA → 2023 rapprochement → February 2026? | drafted |
| Q12.3 | How did Iran's Hormuz weapon shape pre-war Gulf strategy? | drafted |
| **Q12.4** | **Why did MBS-private + UAE-public push for regime change while declining military support to reopen Hormuz?** | **chapter live — [read it](q12-4-gulf-paradox.qmd)** |
| **Q12.5** | **How is the strategic configuration evolving post-war?** | **chapter live — [read it](q12-5-post-war-reconfiguration.qmd)** |

Q12.5's most distinctive finding — a Saudi-led Sunni-Muslim "third pole" that the standard five-configuration menu cannot accommodate — is the chapter that most pushes the framework beyond canonical IR literature.

## Note on Q4

The original Q4 ("what sustains the coalitions?") was answered through cross-coverage in Q11 (US-Israel coalition), Q12.4 / Q12.5 (Gulf), Q9 (Europe-US), Q2 (Iran-side regime-survival as proxy network's structural driver), and Q7 (Russia-NK supply-chain dimension). With the original question fully addressed in the cross-coverage, Q4 has been redefined as a feasibility analysis of the US-led counter-blockade — the only major operational question the existing chapters did not engage directly.
